newsitem.title: USA: Philip Morris says claims laws "unrealistic".
newsitem.headline: Philip Morris says claims laws "unrealistic".

text.p: Philip Morris Companies Inc chairman and chief executive officer said on Monday that legislation proposed to settle smoking and health claims against the tobacco industry was "unrealistic."
Geoffrey Bible also said the company's share price did not reflect its strong businesses because investors were concerned about litigation facing the tobacco industry.
Bible said in the company's mid-year report to shareholders that the company took the tobacco litigation seriously and would fight it vigorously.
"We are devoting all the appropriate resources to fighting the litigation against us," Bible said. "We continue to believe in the strength of our company's defenses."
Bible also referred to recent reports of a proposal for a comprehensive legislative solution to smoking and health claims against the tobacco industry.

"We did not initiate the proposal and we view it as unrealistic," he said. "While we believe that any such legislation would involve significant and perhaps insurmountable difficulties in reconciling the views of many competing interests, we will explore all reasonable measures that may be in the best interests of our shareholders."
Bible reiterated Philip Morris's opposition to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration's assertion of jurisdiction over cigarettes as "unauthorized and illegal."
The chairman described Philip Morris's results for the first six months ending June 30 as "outstanding."
"The first half was a blockbuster," Bible was quoted as saying in the report. "We delivered absolutely phenomonal results."
Results were driven by outstanding volume gains and sustainable income growth in the North American food division, Philip Morris said.
Philip Morris earned $1.97 per share in the second quarter against $1.67 in the same period last year.
